definitions.explanation: Something that is eaten for nourishment.

examples.japanese: {好|す}きな{食|た}べ{物|もの}は{何|なん}ですか。
{日本|にほん}の{食|た}べ{物|もの}はおいしい。
{辛|から}い{食|た}べ{物|もの}が{好|す}きです。
{甘|あま}い{食|た}べ{物|もの}は{体|からだ}によくない。
examples.english: Sweet food isn't good for your body.

examples.japanese: {旅行|りょこう}に{行|い}くと、その{国|くに}の{食|た}べ{物|もの}を{食|た}べてみたい。
examples.english: When I travel, I want to try the food of that country.

notes:
{食|た}べ{物|もの} is the general everyday word for food, referring to anything that can be eaten. It is the most common and neutral term.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {食|た}べ{物|もの}: food in general (everyday, broad)
- {料理|りょうり}: cooking, cuisine, a prepared dish
- {食事|しょくじ}: a meal (the act of eating or a sitting)
- {食品|しょくひん}: food products (commercial/industrial context)
- {食料|しょくりょう}: food supplies, provisions

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {好|す}きな{食|た}べ{物|もの}: favorite food
- {甘|あま}い{食|た}べ{物|もの}: sweet food
- {体|からだ}にいい{食|た}べ{物|もの}: food that's good for your body

WORD FORMATION:
Formed from the verb {食|た}べる + {物|もの} (thing). The pattern verb stem + {物|もの} creates nouns meaning "something to [verb]":
- {飲|の}み{物|もの}: something to drink
- {読|よ}み{物|もの}: reading material
- {買|か}い{物|もの}: shopping (things to buy)
